title: Production deploy — security gate capture & go-live checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures the minimal security gate requirements, evidence capture points, and exception handling notes we require for production deploys (hosted, dedicated, private). It is intended as the operational checklist SREs, Release Engineers, and SecOps follow immediately before and after a go-live.

Audience:
- Release Engineers
- SecOps / Compliance reviewers
- Oncall SREs
- Platform owners for the services in the release

Quick notes (working):
- This is a lean checklist (not the entire checklist matrix). We want a small set of machine-verifiable evidence artifacts that map to RBAC v2 decisions and SIEM events.
- If any item is missing, the release can proceed only with an exception TPM (see Exception Flow).
- Keep evidence retention UID in the ticket (SEC-TAG header) so we can attach SIEM extracts to the release ticket.

Preflight (T minus 2 hours):
- Verify RBAC v2 role binding diffs applied: run `rbac-diff --env prod --release $RELEASE_ID` and attach output to the ticket. Expected output: no wildcard service roles added, no new admin-role grants to non-admins.
- Required roles to check: `platform-admin`, `infra-admin`, `sec-audit`, `deployment-bot`, `service-owner`.
- Confirm deployment pipeline service account is scoped correctly (least privilege for image pulls, secret access).
- Confirm KMS/HSM key usage for new secrets: `kms-usage-report --key $KMS_KEY`.

Machine-verifiable evidence (attach to ticket):
1) RBAC Decision Log snapshot (RBAC v2): `rbac-decision-export --since $DEPLOY_WINDOW --id $RELEASE_ID`
   - Required fields: event_ts, request_id, actor_id, principal_type, action, resource, decision(allow/deny), policy_id, justification_hash.
2) Audit log extract (service-level): `audit-export --service $SERVICE --from $START --to $END --format jsonl`
   - Required fields in this extract: timestamp, trace_id, request_id, actor, action, resource, decision, client_ip, user_agent, before_state, after_state.
3) SIEM snapshot (correlated): saved timeline of any matching high-severity alerts triggered during the deploy window (IDS/IPS, suspicious RBAC denies, anomalous token usage).
4) Deployment pipeline job history (immutable): link to CI/CD job with logs and exit codes; include container image digest and signatures.
5) K8s admission webhook decisions if applicable: `admission-log-export --namespace $NAMESPACE` (fields: ts, pod, admission_result, policy_id).

Audit log schema (recommended minimal shape for evidence automation):
- event_ts: RFC3339 timestamp
- trace_id: opaque string linking distributed traces
- request_id: unique per request
- actor: canonical actor id (user:alice or svc:deployment-bot)
- actor_type: system|user|service
- action: verb with resource (e.g., secrets.get, deployments.create, rbacs.bind)
- resource: full resource path (e.g., /projects/redwood/services/llm-api/deployments/123)
- decision: allow|deny|deferred
- policy_id: id of policy evaluated (if any)
- before: short json blob (string) of pre-state (optional)
- after: short json blob (string) of post-state (optional)
- client_ip: ip or cidr
- user_agent: agent string
- k8s_namespace: if applicable
- exec_duration_ms: integer
- log_version: v1 (bumped when schema changes)

Notes on schema differences vs. previous audits:
- We need `decision` explicit (not inferred from status).
- `policy_id` must be present to tie decisions to RBAC v2 heuristics (policy_id may be composite: rbacv2::12345).
- Keep `before` and `after` short (no full dumps). Use references to S3/object-store keys for large diffs.

SIEM export guidance:
- Exports should be in JSONL. Each line must include the audit schema above plus `siem_event_id` and `siem_severity` (low/med/high/critical).
- Export window default: release start minus 15min to release end plus 15min.
- Label exported file name with release id and retention tag: `siem_export_prod_$RELEASE_ID_rt30d.jsonl` (rt30d indicates retention 30 days in the evidence bundle).
- For automation: `siem-extract --query "trace_id:$TRACE_ID OR request_id:$REQ_ID" --out $PATH`

Evidence automation hooks (how we collect and attach):
- Release pipeline will call `evidence-collector` job after successful deployment stage. It takes release id and query keys.
- Collector will gather: RBAC export, audit logs, CI job logs, SIEM extract, KMS usage report, container signature file.
- Collector outputs a single tar.gz with `manifest.jsonl` index (manifest must include file checksums and minimal metadata).
- Manifest fields (manifest is freeform but automation expects): release_id, created_ts, files: list-of-objects (filename, sha256, type-tag). For now we store manifest as a text blob in the release ticket.

Acceptance criteria (automatic):
- No `deny` decisions for legitimate deployment actions from `deployment-bot` (if there are denies, attach justification and open SEC exception flow).
- No high/critical SIEM alerts during window except those with pre-registered IOC tags listed in the release ticket.
- KMS access only by expected principals (compare KMS usage report to allowlist).
- Images deployed have valid signatures and hash matches the CI artifact published digest.

Manual checks (human):
- Security reviewer confirms no new admin-scoped roles were created for service accounts.
- Security reviewer validates any RBAC policy changes in the PR and signs off in the ticket.
- Product/PM confirms feature flags and kill-switches are present where required.

Exception flow (fast-track):
- If any evidence item fails auto-checks, request an exception with: SEC-EXC-<auto-id> created in JIRA and assigned to SecOps on-call.
- Required for exception: brief risk memo (1 paragraph), mitigation steps (how to rollback), monitoring hooks enabled, expected duration of exception, list of compensating controls.
- Exception approval steps: SecOps reviewer thumbs-up (can be a Slack signoff + link) + production deploy owner acceptance. For anything >24h requires engineering manager + security director approval.

Post-deploy (T plus 15–60 minutes):
- Confirm all expected SIEM events present and matching trace_id.
- Confirm no new 5xx spike in downstream services (dashboards: infra->latency and errors).
- Collect and attach final evidence bundle to the release ticket.
- If any anomaly, open SEC-INC ticket and run escalation.

Operational runbooks and quick commands (appendix):
- RBAC diff: `rbac-diff --env prod --release $RELEASE_ID > /tmp/rbac-diff-$RELEASE_ID.txt`
- Export audit: `audit-export --service llm-api --from $START --to $END --format jsonl > /tmp/audit-$RELEASE_ID.jsonl`
- SIEM extract by trace_id: `siem-extract --query "trace_id:$TRACE_ID" --out /tmp/siem-$RELEASE_ID.jsonl`
- Evidence collector run (local): `evidence-collector --release $RELEASE_ID --attach --out /tmp/evidence-bundle-$RELEASE_ID.tar.gz`

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we require signed manifest (not just checksum) for evidence bundles? (Sana)
- Make `manifest.jsonl` machine-schema stricter (currently freeform). Need to finalize by Q4.
- Confirm retention policy defaults for evidence bundles (30 days vs 90 days) and map to ticket labels (Liam).
- Automate KMS usage allowlist comparison (INFRA ownership).

References and related artifacts:
- Confluence: Deployment Gates - Overview (linked above)
- RBAC v2 spec draft (internal): confluence link in ticket SEC-4123
- Existing audit schema exporters: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-tools (see audit-export)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive on the minimal machine-verifiable fields to speed automated gating and reduce noisy manual checks.
- If you add extra fields to the schema, please add `log_version: v2` and include a migration note in the manifest.

Minor changelog:
- 2024-09-18: initial draft (Asha)
- 2024-09-25: added SIEM file naming convention and manifest guidance (Liam)
- 2024-10-02: clarified RBAC decision fields and exception approval thresholds (Riley)

-- end of doc --
